newsitem.title: USA: Calpine sets financing for Texas power plant.
newsitem.headline: Calpine sets financing for Texas power plant.

text.p: Calpine Corp, based in San Jose, Calif., said Monday it closed $150 million in non-recourse financing for the development of a 240-megawatt (MW) gas-fired "merchant" power plant in Pasadena, Texas.
A merchant power plant is a facility which sells electricity directly to the wholesale power market without the majority of its output being sold under long-term contract.
Calpine will develop, own and operate the facility, which will be built next to the Phillips Petroleum Houston Chemical Complex in Pasadena.
ING Capital, a subsidiary of ING Group, is providing the project construction financing.
When the plant is completed in 1998, around 90 MW of electricity and roughly 200,000 pounds per hour of steam will be supplies to the Phillips chemical plant under a 20-year contract.
Calpine will market the remaining electricity to the Texas market.
Calpine said it recently entered into a 15-year agreement with Aquila Energy of Omaha, Neb., to purchase 45,000 million Btu per day of clean burning natural gas to fuel the facility.
